q: Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in temperature.
e: True. Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in temperature. Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.

q: Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in pressure.
e: False. The claim puts pressure where temperature belongs. Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in temperature. Heat is energy on the move because temperatures differ, not because pressures differ.

q: As heat is a form of energy, heat can be measured in energy unit.
e: True. As heat is a form of energy, heat can be measured in energy unit. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: The unit of heat is joule (J) in SI unit.
e: True. The unit of heat is joule (J) in SI unit. Heat is energy, so the SI unit is the joule.

q: The unit of heat is calorie (cal) in the SI system.
e: False. SI heat is the joule. The calorie is CGS, not SI.

q: Other heat units are calorie (cal) in the CGS system and kilocalorie (kcal) in the MKS system.
e: True. Other heat units are calorie (cal) in the CGS system and kilocalorie (kcal) in the MKS system. CGS still uses the calorie for heat.

q: The heat unit in British system is the British thermal unit (Btu).
e: True. The heat unit in British system is the British thermal unit (Btu). The British heat unit is the Btu.

q: Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 kilocalorie.
e: True. Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 kilocalorie. One kilocalorie raises 1 kg of water by 1 K. That is the MKS heat unit.

q: Heat required to change the temperature of 1 gram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 kilocalorie.
e: False. The claim puts gram where kilogram belongs. Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 kilocalorie. One calorie, not one kilocalorie, raises 1 g of water by 1 K.

q: The German doctor, Robert Mayer, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is 4.184 J.
e: True. The German doctor, Robert Mayer, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is 4.184 J. Mayer's mechanical equivalent of heat is 1 cal = 4.184 J.

q: The relations between heat units are $1 \text{ kcal} = 4184 \text{ J} = 10^3 \text{ cal}$.
e: True. The relations between heat units are 1 kcal = 4184 J = 10³ cal. 1 kW = 10³ W and 1 MW = 10⁶ W.

q: The relations between heat units are $1 \text{ Btu} = 1055 \text{ J}$.
e: True. The relations between heat units are 1 Btu = 1055 J. 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J.

q: The relations between heat units are $1 \text{ ft-lb} = 1.356 \text{ J}$.
e: True. The relations between heat units are 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J.
